title: Family-centered intervention for developmental speech-language disorders using individualized phoneme-enhanced audiobooks for home use
summary:
Treatment of speech sound disorders is among the most common therapies in childhood. In most cases, speech-language therapy is prescribed once a week for 45 minutes. Many children with speech sound difficulties struggle to identify individual speech sounds within the speech signal or to distinguish them from similar-sounding phonemes. As a result, they are unable to use the correct sounds in the appropriate contexts. Some children also have difficulty producing specific sounds, such as “k,” or “g.” These children often exhibit deficits in speech processing as well.
Because speech-language therapy typically takes place only once per week, it would be desirable for parents to support the speech-language learning at home—particularly with regard to speech processing. This may be facilitated through the use of individually tailored audiobook stories, especially when specific phoneme enhancement is applied.
conditions: Specific developmental disorders of speech and language

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age 3;0–6;0 years
- First language: German
- Non-verbal IQ ≥ 85
- Bilateral normal peripheral hearing (percentage hearing loss < 20%; Boenninghaus & Röser, 1973)
- Children with pDLD: diagnosis according to standard criteria for phonological speech sound disorders (german S3 guideline for the treatment of speech developmental disorders)
Exclusion criteria:
- Neuropsychiatric disorders
- Childhood apraxia of speech
- Lack of parental consent
- History of neurosurgical interventions
- Use of medications affecting brain activity
